# Kimball STAR Schema Guidelines

Companion reference for the [`kimball-dbml`](skill.md) skill. Distilled, domain-agnostic Kimball best practices for designing a dimensional model from raw source tables.

> Read this once **before** authoring any dbml. The skill walks you through applying these rules step-by-step.

---

## 1. Naming Conventions

| Object                       | Convention                      | Example                                                                    |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tables, columns, schemas     | `snake_case`                    | `dim_customer`, `is_active`, `marketing_dwh`                               |
| Surrogate key                | `<entity>_key`                  | `customer_key`, `date_key`                                                 |
| Natural / business key       | `<entity>_id` (or domain term)  | `customerid`, `subscription_guid`, `email_address`                         |
| Foreign key                  | Same as the dim's surrogate key | `customer_key` in `fct_sales` references `dim_customer.customer_key`       |
| Boolean                      | `is_*` prefix                   | `is_active`, `is_dropped`, `is_row_effective`                              |
| Date column                  | `<event>_date`                  | `order_date`, `created_date`                                               |
| Date FK                      | `<role>_date_key`               | `order_date_key`, `ship_date_key` (role-playing)                           |
| Dimension table              | `dim_<noun>`                    | `dim_product`, `dim_customer`                                              |
| Fact table                   | `fct_<noun>`                    | `fct_sales`, `fct_pageview`                                                |
| One-big-table (denormalized) | `obt_<noun>`                    | `obt_sales` (fact + conformed dims pre-joined for DirectLake / wide reads) |
| Snapshot table               | `snap_<dim>`                    | `snap_customer`                                                            |
| Bridge table                 | `<a>_<b>_bridge`                | `customer_subscription_bridge`                                             |
| Staging model                | `stg_<source>__<entity>`        | `stg_jaffle_shop__customers`                                               |

**Convert any source-system casing**: `CustomerName` → `customer_name`, `SQLDatabaseGUID` → `sql_database_guid`, `tpid_Str` → `tpid_str`.

---

## 2. STAR Schema Fundamentals

A star schema is a **fact table at the center**, surrounded by **dimension tables** joined via integer surrogate keys.

```
        dim_date         dim_product
            \                /
             \              /
              \            /
        ┌──────────────────────┐
        │     fct_sales        │
        │  - date_key (FK)     │
        │  - product_key (FK)  │
        │  - customer_key (FK) │
        │  - revenue (measure) │
        │  - quantity (measure)│
        └──────────────────────┘
              /            \
             /              \
        dim_customer       dim_<other>
```

Rules of thumb:

- **Facts hold keys and measures only.** Never descriptive attributes.
- **Dimensions hold descriptive attributes.** Never measures (with rare exceptions like `is_active` flags that drive filters).
- **Always join via the surrogate key.** Integer comparisons are fast, immune to source-system encoding drift.
- **The grain is sacred.** Document it in the table's `Note:` and never change it without a new fact table.

---

## 3. Surrogate vs Natural Keys

- **Surrogate key** (`<entity>_key`): integer or short string, generated by the warehouse. Used for **all joins**.
- **Natural key** (`<entity>_id`): the source-system business identifier. Kept on the dimension for **display / lookup**, never for joins.

```sql
-- ✅ Correct: surrogate key join
SELECT c.customer_name, SUM(f.revenue)
FROM fct_sales f
INNER JOIN dim_customer c ON f.customer_key = c.customer_key
GROUP BY c.customer_name;

-- ❌ Wrong: natural key join (slow, fragile to source changes)
SELECT c.customer_name, SUM(f.revenue)
FROM fct_sales f
INNER JOIN dim_customer c ON UPPER(f.customer_email) = UPPER(c.customer_email);
```

In dbt, generate surrogate keys with `{{ dbt_utils.generate_surrogate_key(['natural_key_cols']) }}` — never `ROW_NUMBER()` (unstable across runs).

---

## 4. Unknown-Member Pattern

Every dimension should have a single row with **surrogate key = `-1`** representing "unknown / unassigned / not applicable":

| customer_key | customer_name | customer_email    |
| ------------ | ------------- | ----------------- |
| -1           | (Unknown)     | (Unknown)         |
| 1            | Alice         | alice@example.com |
| 2            | Bob           | bob@example.com   |

Benefits:

- **Facts always have a non-null FK** → use `INNER JOIN`, never `LEFT JOIN`, into dimensions
- Replaces sentinel checks: `customer_key <> -1` is faster + clearer than `email IS NOT NULL AND email <> '' AND email <> 'unknown'`
- Referential integrity is preserved without nulls

---

## 5. Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD)

| Type     | What changes                               | When to use                                                                     |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **SCD0** | Never (immutable)                          | `dim_date`, lookup tables that don't drift                                      |
| **SCD1** | Overwrite — only the current value matters | When historical tracking is unnecessary (e.g. a typo fix in `customer_name`)    |
| **SCD2** | Track full history with new rows           | When point-in-time queries matter (e.g. customer segment changed on 2024-06-01) |
| **SCD3** | Add a `previous_*` column (rare)           | When you only care about one prior value                                        |
| **SCD6** | Hybrid 1+2+3                               | Specialized use cases                                                           |

### SCD2 column requirements

Every SCD2 dimension MUST include:

```sql
row_effective_start  DATE          -- when this version became active
row_effective_end    DATE          -- when this version stopped (high date like 9999-12-31 for current)
is_row_effective     BOOLEAN       -- true for the current version (filter on this)
```

Plus the business key (so multiple versions of the same entity can be linked):

```sql
<entity>_natural_id  VARCHAR       -- e.g. customer_email, sql_database_guid
```

**Always filter on `is_row_effective = TRUE`** when querying current state:

```sql
SELECT c.segment_name, COUNT(*)
FROM dim_customer c
WHERE c.is_row_effective = TRUE
GROUP BY c.segment_name;
```

### dbt mapping

- **SCD2 dims** → use [dbt snapshots](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/snapshots) (`strategy: timestamp` or `check`), then `ref()` the snapshot in `dim_*`
- **SCD1 dims** → regular `dim_*.sql` model, full refresh or incremental upsert
- **SCD0 dims** → regular `dim_*.sql`, seed file, or DBT macro (e.g. `dbt_date.get_date_dimension(...)`)

---

## 6. Fact Table Archetypes

| Archetype                 | Grain                                                             | Use for                                                     | Measure additivity                                                                  |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Transaction**           | One row per event                                                 | Atomic events — orders, clicks, page views, login attempts  | Fully additive across all dims                                                      |
| **Periodic snapshot**     | One row per (entity, period)                                      | Daily/weekly/monthly state — inventory counts, balances     | ❌ Counts/balances NOT additive across time; ✅ accumulated measures (CU-hours) are |
| **Accumulating snapshot** | One row per process instance (updated as it moves through stages) | Order fulfillment, application pipelines, claims processing | Mixed; document per measure                                                         |
| **Factless fact**         | One row per event with NO measure                                 | Membership, eligibility, attendance                         | Count rows only                                                                     |
| **Aggregated fact**       | One row per (dim combination, period)                             | Pre-rolled product-level / customer-level KPIs              | Usually fully additive                                                              |

### Periodic snapshot additivity — the rule that traps everyone

For a **periodic snapshot fact** (one row per entity per day):

| Measure type                                         | Additive across time? | Query pattern                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Counts** (entities, customers)                     | ❌ NO                 | Filter to a specific date: `WHERE date_key = (SELECT MAX(date_key) FROM <fact>)` |
| **State / balances** (storage size, inventory level) | ❌ NO                 | Filter to a specific date                                                        |
| **Accumulated** (consumption units, hours, revenue)  | ✅ YES                | `SUM(...)` across the date range                                                 |

```sql
-- ✅ Correct: latest snapshot for current count
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_key)
FROM fct_daily_inventory
WHERE date_key = (SELECT MAX(date_key) FROM fct_daily_inventory);

-- ❌ Wrong: double-counts customers appearing on multiple days
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_key)
FROM fct_daily_inventory
WHERE date_key >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL 28 DAY;

-- ✅ Correct: SUM additive measure across range
SELECT SUM(consumption_units)
FROM fct_daily_inventory
WHERE date_key >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL 28 DAY;
```

---

## 7. Role-Playing Dimensions

When the same dimension plays multiple roles in one fact (most commonly `dim_date`), use **descriptive aliases** for the FK column:

```dbml
Table fct_order_fulfillment {
    order_date_key   varchar [note: 'FK to dim_date — when order was placed']
    ship_date_key    varchar [note: 'FK to dim_date — when order shipped']
    deliver_date_key varchar [note: 'FK to dim_date — when order was delivered']
    customer_key     varchar
    revenue          decimal
}

Ref: dim_date.date_key < fct_order_fulfillment.order_date_key
Ref: dim_date.date_key < fct_order_fulfillment.ship_date_key
Ref: dim_date.date_key < fct_order_fulfillment.deliver_date_key
```

In SQL, alias the dimension per role:

```sql
SELECT od.date AS order_date, sd.date AS ship_date, f.revenue
FROM fct_order_fulfillment f
INNER JOIN dim_date od ON f.order_date_key = od.date_key
INNER JOIN dim_date sd ON f.ship_date_key  = sd.date_key;
```

---

## 8. Bridge Tables for Many-to-Many

When entity A maps to many B's _and_ vice versa (e.g. customer ↔ subscription, user ↔ role, post ↔ tag), use a **bridge table**:

```dbml
Table customer_subscription_bridge {
    customer_subscription_bridge_key varchar [primary key]
    customer_key                      varchar [not null]
    subscription_key                  varchar [not null]
    is_row_effective                  bool
    row_effective_start               date
    row_effective_end                 date
}

Ref: dim_customer.customer_key      < customer_subscription_bridge.customer_key
Ref: dim_subscription.subscription_key < customer_subscription_bridge.subscription_key
```

- Bridge is itself **not** SCD2 (it's rebuilt each run from latest effective versions of A and B), but it should include `is_row_effective` so you can filter to current state.
- For weighted relationships (e.g. customer A is 60% owner of subscription X), add a `weight` column.

---

## 9. Conformed Dimensions (the Bus Matrix)

A **conformed dimension** is one that's identical (same surrogate keys, same attributes) across multiple fact tables. The full set of conformed dims + facts forms the **enterprise bus matrix**:

|                  | fct_sales | fct_returns | fct_pageview |
| ---------------- | :-------: | :---------: | :----------: |
| **dim_date**     |     ✓     |      ✓      |      ✓       |
| **dim_customer** |     ✓     |      ✓      |      ✓       |
| **dim_product**  |     ✓     |      ✓      |      —       |
| **dim_session**  |     —     |      —      |      ✓       |

Rules:

- Conformed dims live at the **lowest schema** (e.g. `dbo.` or root) so any fact can join them.
- Subject-area-specific dims live alongside their fact (e.g. `sql_paas.database_dim`).
- **DRY**: a new fact should reuse conformed dims first; only invent new local dims when the new fact needs attributes that don't fit any conformed dim's grain.

---

## 10. Date Dimension (`dim_date`)

Every star schema needs a `dim_date`. Minimum columns:

```dbml
Table dim_date {
    Note: 'One row per calendar date. SCD0 (immutable). Unknown member at date_key = -1.'
    date_key            varchar [primary key, note: '{{META:NATURAL_KEY}} yyyymmdd as a string']
    date                date
    day                 integer
    day_of_week         integer
    day_of_week_name    varchar
    day_of_month        integer
    day_of_year         integer
    week_of_year        integer
    iso_week_of_year    integer
    month               integer
    month_name          varchar
    quarter             integer
    quarter_name        varchar
    year                integer
    first_day_of_month  date
    last_day_of_month   date
    first_day_of_year   date
    last_day_of_year    date
    is_weekend          bool
}
```

Power BI: set `data_category: Time` on the `date` column to enable time intelligence. Make it a contiguous range covering all facts.

dbt: use [`dbt_date.get_date_dimension`](https://github.com/calogica/dbt-date) or a seed file — never hand-roll.

---

## 11. dbml Authoring Conventions (This Repo)

The skill emits an **authoring-style** dbml (rich notes, intentional design) — distinct from the **generated-style** dbml that `dbterd` produces from a compiled dbt manifest.

### Table block

```dbml
Table dim_customer {
    Note: 'One row per customer. SCD2 — filter is_row_effective = true for current state. Unknown member at customer_key = -1.'
    customer_key         varchar [primary key]
    customer_natural_id  varchar [note: '{{META:NATURAL_KEY}} Email address normalized to lowercase, used for deduplication across sources']
    customer_name        varchar
    customer_segment     varchar [note: '{{META:SCD2}}']
    industry             varchar [note: '{{META:SCD2}}']
    row_effective_start  date
    row_effective_end    date
    is_row_effective     bool
}
```

### Meta flags (in column `note:`)

| Flag                   | Meaning                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `{{META:NATURAL_KEY}}` | This column is the source-system business identifier. Use for lookup/display, not for joins.                         |
| `{{META:SCD2}}`        | This attribute is tracked over time. Changes create a new row.                                                       |
| `{{META:ROLE_PLAYED}}` | This FK is a role-playing reference (e.g. `ship_date_key` → `dim_date`).                                             |
| `{{META:DEGENERATE}}`  | This is a degenerate dimension — a high-cardinality key stored on the fact, no separate dim table (e.g. `order_id`). |

### References block (always at the bottom)

```dbml
// ============================================================
// References
// ============================================================

Ref: dim_date.date_key < fct_sales.order_date_key
Ref: dim_customer.customer_key < fct_sales.customer_key
Ref: dim_product.product_key < fct_sales.product_key
```

Read `Ref: A.col < B.col` as: "A is the parent (1) — B is the child (many)". dbdiagram.io renders this as a 1-to-many crow's-foot.

### Schema namespacing

Use `Table <schema>.<name>` when the model spans multiple schemas (e.g. shared conformed dims in `dbo.` and subject-area facts in `sql_paas.`). For a single-schema model, just `Table <name>`.

### Section markers

Order matters for readability:

```dbml
// ============================================================
// Conformed Dimensions
// ============================================================
Table dim_date { ... }
Table dim_customer { ... }

// ============================================================
// Local Dimensions
// ============================================================
Table dim_product { ... }
Table dim_session { ... }

// ============================================================
// Facts
// ============================================================
Table fct_post { ... }
Table fct_comment { ... }

// ============================================================
// Bridge Tables
// ============================================================
Table post_tag_bridge { ... }

// ============================================================
// References
// ============================================================
Ref: ...
```

---

## 12. Common Anti-Patterns

- ❌ **Descriptive attributes on facts** (`customer_name` on `fct_sales`). They belong on `dim_customer`.
- ❌ **Natural keys for joins** (`f.customer_email = c.customer_email`). Use surrogate keys.
- ❌ **`LEFT JOIN` into a dim** when the unknown-member pattern is in place. Use `INNER JOIN` — `-1` covers nulls.
- ❌ **Summing counts across days** on a periodic snapshot fact. Filter to a single date.
- ❌ **`SELECT DISTINCT`** to dedup a join result. Properly designed STARs with `is_row_effective` filters don't need it.
- ❌ **Hardcoded `database.table` references** in dbt. Always `{{ ref(...) }}` / `{{ source(...) }}`.
- ❌ **Changing a fact's grain** without renaming it. The grain is part of the contract.
- ❌ **Bi-directional relationships** (Power BI). Use only when ambiguity is unavoidable AND you've accepted the perf cost.
- ❌ **One huge fact table per source system** ("the kitchen sink"). Split by grain and process.
- ❌ **Skipping `dim_date`**. Always include one, even if every other dim is degenerate.
